senses.definition: A time when people have a break from school or work, often spent traveling or resting.
senses.example: During our vacation we visited a lake.

senses.definition: A space with little or no matter, such as air or another gas.
senses.example: Sound cannot travel across a perfect vacuum.

senses.definition: A machine that draws in air to collect dust and dirt from a surface.
senses.example: The vacuum picked up the crumbs under the table.

senses.definition: To clean a surface using a machine that draws in air and dirt.
senses.example: I vacuumed the carpet after the party.

senses.definition: A bottle with very little matter between two walls to slow the flow of heat into or out of it.
senses.example: The cold water in our vacuum bottle was still cold at lunchtime.

senses.definition: A machine that uses moving air to pick up loose dirt and collect it in a bag or bin.
senses.example: The vacuum cleaner picked up crumbs from the rug.

senses.definition: Too proud of how you look or what you can do.
senses.example: The vain prince kept asking everyone to admire his shoes.

senses.definition: Without success or useful results, especially in the phrase in vain.
senses.example: I searched in vain for the key I had already put in my pocket.

senses.definition: A low area between hills or mountains, often with a river running through it.
senses.example: A stream curved along the valley.

senses.definition: Worth a lot of money or important enough to save and protect.
senses.example: The old book was valuable because it belonged to the town’s first library.

senses.definition: An expensive or important item, usually used in the plural.
senses.example: The travelers kept their valuables in a small bag.

senses.definition: How light or dark a color looks in a work of art.
senses.example: The pale blue and the dark blue had different values.

senses.definition: A part that opens or closes to control where liquid or gas moves.
senses.example: A valve in your heart closes to keep blood from moving backward.

senses.definition: A closed road vehicle with room to carry people or goods.
senses.example: We loaded the boxes into the back of the van.

senses.definition: To disappear or stop being seen.
senses.example: The deer vanished into the trees.

senses.definition: A point in a drawing where lines heading into the distance seem to meet.
senses.example: The artist drew the hall’s edges toward one vanishing point.

senses.definition: In programming, a name used to keep track of a value a program needs.
senses.example: The program keeps the team’s score in a variable.

senses.definition: A group made up of different kinds of things or people.
senses.example: We saw a variety of birds near the lake.

senses.definition: One particular kind of something that comes in different forms.
senses.example: This variety of apple stays green even when it is ripe.

senses.definition: A container, usually taller than it is wide, made for holding flowers or as decoration.
senses.example: We put three flowers in the blue vase.

senses.definition: Very large in size, amount, or area.
senses.example: The road crossed a vast, flat plain.

senses.definition: A saved picture described as shapes and lines that can be drawn again at different sizes.
senses.example: The vector image of a circle stayed smooth when we made it bigger.

senses.definition: Something made to carry people or goods, especially on roads but also on rails, water, or in the air.
senses.example: The road was too narrow for a large vehicle to turn around.

senses.definition: A tube that carries blood back toward the heart.
senses.example: A vein in my leg brings blood toward my heart.

senses.definition: An oval track made for bicycle racing.
senses.example: The cyclists leaned into a bend at the velodrome.

senses.definition: A soft cloth with very short threads standing up close together on one side.
senses.example: Soft velvet covered the inside of the box.

senses.definition: A thin sheet of wood that can be glued onto something or pressed together with other sheets.
senses.example: The plywood had a smooth veneer on its top layer.

senses.definition: An opening that lets air, gas, or steam enter or escape.
senses.example: Warm air came through the vent near the floor.

senses.definition: To let out a gas, air, or strong feelings.
senses.example: After the game, I called a friend to vent about losing the last point.

senses.definition: A word that tells what someone or something does, what happens, or what state something is in.
senses.example: Jumped, seems, and grew can all be verbs.

senses.definition: The decision a jury or judge gives at the end of a trial.
senses.example: The judge read the verdict aloud after everyone returned.

senses.definition: A shallow wetland pool that holds water for part of the year and often lacks permanent fish populations.
senses.example: When the forest warmed up in spring, salamanders moved into the vernal pool.

senses.definition: A line of a poem or a group of lines in a song or poem.
senses.example: We learned the first verse of the song before lunch.

senses.definition: One of the bones that form the spine.
senses.example: Each vertebra helps protect the spinal cord.

senses.definition: A point where sides or edges meet, like the corner of a triangle or box.
senses.example: Each vertex of the box touches three edges.

senses.definition: Going straight up and down.
senses.example: Draw a vertical line from the top of the paper to the bottom.

senses.definition: A piece of clothing worn on the upper body without sleeves.
senses.example: I put on a bright vest before the ride.

senses.definition: An official refusal to approve a plan or proposed law, or the power to refuse that approval.
senses.example: A president’s veto can stop a bill from becoming law unless enough lawmakers vote to pass it anyway.

senses.definition: To use your authority to refuse to approve something.
senses.example: A president may veto a bill after lawmakers pass it.

senses.definition: A quick back-and-forth or up-and-down movement that repeats.
senses.example: I felt the vibration of the drum when I touched its edge.

senses.definition: An act of winning a contest or overcoming a challenge.
senses.example: The team cheered after its first victory of the season.

senses.definition: A recording or display of moving images, often with sound.
senses.example: We watched a video that showed how to fold a paper boat.

senses.definition: What you can see from a place.
senses.example: From the hill we had a view of the whole town.

senses.definition: A way of thinking about a question or situation.
senses.example: The two speakers had different views of how to solve the problem.

senses.definition: To look at or watch something.
senses.example: Visitors can view the painting from the other side of the rope.

senses.definition: A small community of homes and other buildings, usually smaller than a town.
senses.example: A narrow road led from the village to the coast.

senses.definition: A small stringed instrument usually held under the chin and played by moving a bow across its four strings.
senses.example: I heard the violin begin the tune on its own.

senses.definition: Able to be seen.
senses.example: After the fog lifted, the distant lighthouse was visible again.

senses.definition: To go somewhere or spend time with someone and then leave again.
senses.example: We visited our cousins last Saturday.

senses.definition: A time spent going to a place or seeing a person.
senses.example: Our visit to the train museum lasted an hour.

senses.definition: A person who comes to a place or sees someone for a short time.
senses.example: A visitor asked us where to find the picnic tables.

senses.definition: A substance from food or another source that your body needs in small quantities for its usual work.
senses.example: Different vegetables can supply different vitamins.

senses.definition: Very bright or clear, or easy to picture in your mind.
senses.example: Her vivid story made me feel like I could see the orange cliffs.

senses.definition: The words someone knows or uses, or the words used for a certain subject or language.
senses.example: We made a vocabulary list before reading about the ocean.

senses.definition: A pouch under the throat of some animals, including many frogs, that can fill with air and help them make loud calls.
senses.example: The spring peeper’s vocal sac puffed up as it called.

senses.definition: The sound a person makes when speaking or singing.
senses.example: Her voice was so soft that I moved closer to hear.

senses.definition: A chance or power to express what you think.
senses.example: Everyone in the club has a voice in choosing our next book.

senses.definition: To say what you think or feel openly.
senses.example: Several students voiced concern about the slippery steps.

senses.definition: An opening in Earth’s surface through which hot rock, ash, and gas can escape. The word can also mean the mountain that builds up around the opening.
senses.example: The volcano’s last eruption left a new layer of rock.

senses.definition: In games such as tennis or soccer, a hit or kick made before the ball touches the ground.
senses.example: Her tennis volley went over the net before the ball had a chance to bounce.

senses.definition: To hit or kick a ball before it touches the ground.
senses.example: I stepped forward to volley the ball back.

senses.definition: A measure of the difference in electric energy per unit of charge between two places. It can help drive electric current.
senses.example: The small battery has a lower voltage than the source of power for a house.

senses.definition: The amount of space something takes up, or the amount a container can hold.
senses.example: We measured the volume of the tank in liters.

senses.definition: A person who offers to do work or help without being required to do it, often without pay.
senses.example: A volunteer read stories aloud at the library.

senses.definition: To offer to do a task or give information without waiting to be asked.
senses.example: I volunteered to collect the game pieces.

senses.definition: A choice recorded in a group decision or election.
senses.example: Each member had one vote for the next club leader.

senses.definition: To show or record a choice in a group decision or election.
senses.example: We voted on which playground game to try first.

senses.definition: A speech sound made with air flowing freely through the mouth, or a letter used to write such a sound.
senses.example: The word map has a vowel sound between two consonants.

senses.definition: A small mark placed near a letter in some writing systems to show a vowel sound.
senses.example: The book for new readers showed the vowel point below the Hebrew letter.

senses.definition: A long journey, especially by sea or through space.
senses.example: The explorers packed supplies for their voyage across the ocean.
